prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

LONDON, England (CNN) -- Kimi Raikkonen has lambasted McLaren's Lewis Hamilton for the pit-lane accident that ended both of their races at the Canadian Grand Prix. Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen is far from happy after Lewis Hamilton  pushed him out of the Canadian Grand Prix. Hamilton's McLaren rammed into the back of world champion Raikkonen's Ferrari as the Finn and Robert Kubica, the race's eventual winner, were waiting at a red light after the safety car was forced into action on lap 17. Raikkonen, while claiming not to be angry, was clearly far from impressed. "There's not much I can say. My race was ruined by Hamilton's mistake. "Obviously, anyone can make mistakes, as I did two weeks ago in Monaco, but it's one thing to make a mistake at 200 hundred [miles] per hour but another to hit a car stopped at a red light. "I'm not angry because that doesn't achieve anything and does not change my result. I am unhappy because I had a great chance of winning." Raikkonen, who has failed to score points in the previous two races, said he had to start winning again. "There is still a long way to go in the championship and it is still very close and we have everything we need to regain the ground we have lost." Ferrari team sporting director Stefano Domenicali said Hamilton had made a "serious mistake." "I think the penalty imposed by the FIA [Hamilton was given a 10-place grid penalty for the French Grand Prix at Magny-Cours] is in line with it, even if it does not restore what was a lost opportunity for us. "Kimi was in an excellent position to fight for the win" Hamilton, for his part, was apologetic. "I don't know what happened to be honest," Hamilton said. "I was comfortably in the lead, it was looking like an easy win. Then I went in for the pit stop. It was not a good stop and I saw the two guys in front of me battling in the pit lane. "I saw the red light but by that time it was a bit late. It was not exactly a racing incident as such, it was unfortunate. It was one of those things. It is different to if you crash into the wall and you are angry. It is not like that. I apologize to Kimi for ruining his race."

## Ferrari furious after Hamilton pit-lane error ends Räikkönen’s Canadian Grand Prix

Ferrari were left frustrated and empty-handed in Montreal after Lewis Hamilton crashed into the back of Kimi Räikkönen in the Canadian Grand Prix pit lane, ending the world champion’s race in bizarre fashion and dealing a major blow to Ferrari’s afternoon.

The incident occurred during a pit-stop sequence under safety-car conditions at the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve. Räikkönen had stopped at the pit-lane exit alongside BMW Sauber’s Robert Kubica, obeying the red light while the field passed on the track. Hamilton, exiting his McLaren pit box behind them, failed to slow in time and struck the rear of Räikkönen’s Ferrari, eliminating both cars on the spot.

Nico Rosberg, following behind, also made contact with Hamilton’s McLaren, but it was the collision between Hamilton and Räikkönen that dominated the post-race fallout.

The stewards later handed Hamilton a grid penalty for the following race, judging that the McLaren driver had caused an avoidable collision. But for Ferrari, the penalty did little to ease the sense of a huge opportunity lost.

### Domenicali: Ferrari paid a heavy price

Ferrari team principal Stefano Domenicali made clear that the team regarded the incident as especially costly because Räikkönen had been in a strong position to score heavily — and potentially fight for victory — before being taken out in a non-racing situation.

Domenicali said Ferrari had done what was required tactically during the safety-car phase and that Räikkönen had simply stopped when instructed by the red light at pit exit.

“We are obviously very disappointed,” Domenicali said. “Kimi’s race was ended through no fault of his own. He was stopped at the red light, as the regulations require, and then he was hit from behind. It is frustrating because we had the pace and we were in a position to score important points.”

The Ferrari boss also stressed that the team expected drivers to remain fully alert in the pit lane, particularly under safety-car conditions when the traffic pattern can become complicated.

“In Formula One the smallest mistake can have very big consequences,” he added. “This was one of those moments. Unfortunately, Ferrari and Kimi paid the price.”

### Räikkönen: “There was nothing I could do”

Räikkönen, who had been running competitively before the safety-car reshuffle, was characteristically blunt after the race. The Finn said the situation was simple: the light was red, he stopped, and Hamilton ran into him.

“There is not much to say,” Räikkönen said. “The red light was on, so I stopped. Then I was hit from behind. I could not go anywhere, and there was nothing I could do.”

The reigning world champion was visibly irritated at the scene, gesturing toward the red light after climbing from his damaged Ferrari. His frustration was understandable: the crash not only ended his race but also damaged his championship momentum on a day when Ferrari appeared capable of taking a strong result.

Räikkönen declined to launch into a lengthy criticism of Hamilton, but his point was clear — the accident happened in a controlled area of the circuit where drivers are expected to react to signals and avoid contact.

“It is always disappointing to retire, especially like this,” he said. “We had a good chance today, and it was taken away.”

### Hamilton accepts responsibility

Hamilton accepted responsibility for the collision, admitting he had not seen the stationary cars and the red light early enough to avoid contact.

The McLaren driver had been leading before the pit stops but lost time during the service and emerged behind Räikkönen and Kubica as they waited at the pit exit. He appeared to focus on the cars ahead rather than the pit-lane signal, only realising too late that they had stopped.

“I made a mistake,” Hamilton said. “I saw the two cars in front and I was trying to avoid them, but by the time I realised they were stopped it was too late. I apologise to Kimi and to Ferrari.”

Hamilton said the incident was particularly painful because McLaren had been in contention for victory.

“It is hugely disappointing,” he added. “We had a strong car and I was pushing hard, but these things happen. I will learn from it.”

### Championship implications

The collision had major consequences for the championship picture. Räikkönen’s retirement meant Ferrari lost a strong scoring opportunity, while Hamilton also departed with nothing from a race he had looked capable of winning.

The beneficiary was Robert Kubica, who avoided the chaos and went on to claim a landmark victory for BMW Sauber. His win shook up the title standings and underlined how costly the pit-lane crash had been for both Ferrari and McLaren.

For Ferrari, however, the dominant emotion was irritation. Pit-lane incidents are rare, and to lose a front-running car while stationary at a red light was especially hard to accept.

Domenicali summed up the mood in the Ferrari garage: “We leave Canada knowing we could have achieved much more. The performance was there, but the result was taken away by an incident outside our control. Now we must focus on responding at the next race.”
